hints.title: Match a counterexample to the full statement
hints.body: To refute an IF statement, its premise must hold and its conclusion must fail. To refute a claim of no positive integer solutions, construct one such solution.
hints.recap: A counterexample must satisfy every stated restriction.

solution:
1. Check eligibility. A requires no common divisor greater than one; the given triple has common divisor four.

2. Construct a solution. Since 162=44, the identity becomes 44+122=202. Thus (a,b,c)=(4,12,20) contradicts B.

3. Check the remaining uses. For C, 12 and 20 are not integer squares, so this identity does not give three fourth powers. For D, 16 is exactly the mean of 12 and 20, so the triple supports that particular conclusion.

Answer B. All three inputs in the constructed counterexample are positive integers.
